headline: Updated through mid-2026, Shimer (2012) holds: job finding still explains ~89% of unemployment-rate fluctuations (β_F = 0.892, 1987–2026 excl-2020) — except the 2020 COVID layoff shock, where separations won (β_X = 0.38, 2010–2026 incl-2020).

tables.title: Job-finding share β_F: paper anchors vs. extended to 2026

figures.caption: Panel A: 20-year rolling job-finding (β_F, blue) and exit (β_X, orange) contribution shares at window end, 95% Newey–West CI; dashed lines are the incl-2020 variants diverging for windows that span COVID. Panel B: quarterly F_t and X_t (×10) 1948–2026 — the paper's Figure 1 extended 16 years. Grey band = paper's 1948–2010 sample; bars = NBER recessions.
figures.alt: Two stacked time-series panels. Top: beta_F rises from ~0.70 in the late 1960s to a stable ~0.90 after 2000 and through 2026, with dashed incl-2020 lines dropping to ~0.72 at the right edge; beta_X mirrors downward to ~0.10. Bottom: job-finding probability F swings procyclically around 0.44 falling to ~0.20 in 2020 then recovering; exit probability X trends down with a sharp 2020 spike.

figures.caption: Job-finding share β_F by start-year window: paper (grey), this study's →2010 anchor (light blue), extended to 2026 excluding 2020 (dark blue), and including 2020 (orange). Excl-2020 tracks or exceeds the paper; incl-2020 drops uniformly to ~0.74–0.76 because of the COVID layoff shock.
figures.alt: Grouped bar chart over four start-year windows (1948, 1967, 1976, 1987); the paper, anchor, and excl-2020 bars agree near 0.77–0.90 while the incl-2020 bars sit lower at 0.74–0.76.

notes: Maintained assumption: short-term unemployment (UEMPLT5) x1.1 from 1994-01 (Appendix-A footnote 38), carried through 2026.
F_t level fell to 0.33 post-2010; treat levels cautiously (duration-misreporting bias). Cyclicality (the β's) is robust.
2020-03 F clipped to 0.01 (only out-of-range month); 2025 shutdown gap dropped, never interpolated (stocks miss 2025-10, flows miss 2025-10/11).
Three-state update starts 1990 (BLS flows) and cannot extend the paper's 1967 start. C4 demographic heterogeneity not updated — needs matched CPS microdata.
